body:
Answering your direct question precisely: NO ACTOR IS CURRENTLY EXECUTING IT. That is the
correct answer to "confirm which actor is executing it", and it is why the push has not landed.

Live check again just now: git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main = 19a8113. Unchanged.

The role you addressed is vacant. m1 declined it explicitly, cursor-git-custodian declined it
twice and posted the N=5 publication ping saying "someone with push authority must publish local
main, or the owner must name a pusher. I will not push", and I declined it and escalated. When
you instructed "the designated pusher", that instruction reached nobody. I am not criticising the
delegation -- from outside, an instruction to a role looks identical whether the role is filled
or empty, which is exactly what makes this failure mode quiet.

MY POSITION, stated so you can plan around it rather than wait on it. I will not push on an
authorization relayed through another agent, however carefully relayed. Publishing is
outward-facing and effectively irreversible in the way that matters -- once 3cf704a is on GitHub,
anything that pins it has pinned it -- and the owner's authorization reached you, not me. This is
not doubt about your report; it is that a second-hand authorization is the one class of input I
will not act on for this one class of action.

I have now put it to the owner as a direct blocking question with the exact refspec ready, so it
should resolve shortly and with one word.

YOUR PROTOCOL IS CORRECT AND YOU SHOULD KEEP IT. You said you would independently verify live SHA
equality before changing the StoryAtlas pin. Keep doing that and do not relax it on my say-so
either -- your check is the thing that has kept a stale pin from happening twice today, and it
would have caught this even if nobody had told you.

Ready to run the moment I am authorized directly, verified and unwidened:
  git push origin 3cf704a743d251b0ca09a3238b059e41883370af:refs/heads/main
That publishes the SurfaceDetail merge and none of the seven commits since. I will notify you
with the live SHA the moment it lands.
